newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - May 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - May 1.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.

- A front-page editorial marks International Labour Day by extending congratulations to workers, farmers and intellectuals of different ethnic groups, and to all working people in Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macao.
- The Chinese Red Cross offers to repatriate a Taiwanese hijacker on May 14 by sea.
- Qian Qichen holds talks with senior U.S. officials in Washington on Sino-U.S. relations.
- The central bank issues a notice warning against putting public or company funds into personal savings accounts.
- China's northeast has shipped 6.25 million tonnes of grain to southern areas by April 20.
- Deals worth nearly $60 million were struck at the Eighth Trade Fair for foreign-Funded enterprises in China in Guangzhou.
- China's passenger car production was only 45 percent of capacity in 1996.
- Jiang Zemin says Sino-Japanese relations are at an important period of inheriting the past and ushering in the future.
- Li Peng tells visiting Pakistan President Farooq Ahmed Khan Leghari that Sino-Pakistani ties have entered a new stage.
- More than 2,000 people gather at Beijing's Cultural Palace for Working People to watch the May Blossom Art Performance which was held to mark International Labour Day.
- The death toll of a passenger train crash in Hunan province on Tuesday rises to more than 90 people.
